title: Theo and the Wolf
premise: Ines Dunmore, a bone-carver who hears the dead through the relics she carves, has survived by staying invisible in the smuggler's roads of Thornfell. When the crown's witch-hunters burn her village and she discovers a dying wolf who is not a wolf but the last guardian of Veyra—a country erased from maps and memory—she inherits its unfinished duty: carry the dragon-fire ember that keeps Veyra's door open before it gutters out. Hunted by Captain Aldric Vane, who once loved her and now serves the crown, Ines must choose between saving herself across the border or reopening a door that could free every gifted soul the kingdom has buried. She reopens the door, at the cost of her own hearing—the dead go silent forever—and steps into Veyra with the wolf and the refugees she gathered, founding a new home among ghosts finally at rest.
about_author: Z. M. Sandoval is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent years mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write stories about borders—geographic, magical, and emotional—from a cabin full of animal bones and half-finished maps.

chapters.title: The Bone That Sang
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Carving a commission for a grieving widow, Ines hears the widow's dead son warn of soldiers on the pass. She ignores it until witch-hunters arrive, burn the carving-house, and kill her mentor. Fleeing with only her tools, she finds a wounded silver wolf caught in a hunter's snare—and realizes it speaks with a voice older than any ghost. Beat: terror giving way to reluctant responsibility.

chapters.title: What the Wolf Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Ines and the wolf, Vael. Through shared dreams, Vael shows her Veyra: the country the crown unmade, its people scattered, its door held open by a single dragon-fire ember now guttering in his chest. He names her heir by blood-right—her grandmother was Veyran. Meanwhile Vane tracks them, leaving burned waystations. Beat: wonder curdling into dread as inheritance becomes burden.

chapters.title: The Hunt on Thornfell
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Gathering other marked survivors—a deaf boy who reads bone-vibrations, an old smuggler who owes her—Ines races for the door's location atop the Thornfell spire. Vane corners them; he offers Ines amnesty if she surrenders the ember, revealing the crown fears what lies beyond erased doors. The wolf takes a killing blow meant for her. Beat: betrayal, sacrifice, and the refusal to bargain.

chapters.title: A Door Made of Ash
chapters.summary: Ines's POV, climax to resolution. Cradling the dying wolf, she pours her gift into the ember, using every voice of the dead she has ever heard as kindling. The door opens; Vane, broken by what he witnesses, lets them pass. The dead fall silent as their voices burn—but the refugees cross into Veyra, where the wolf, transformed, waits at a hearth. Beat: grief transmuted into belonging.
